title: What if you were stranded on a frozen mountain with a pilot who goes by the book?
formula: Strange act (digging a ditch inside your own door) -> why (crash, forty below, a week to rescue) -> the doubter with the 'perfect' shelter (Captain Ruth, 40 years flying, the steel plane and the manual) -> weird prep with measured progress (hour stamps, roof hole, the ditch) -> the manual against you -> blizzard setback -> status flip at ~75%: her own steel pulls the heat out of her -> mechanism explained -> knock -> loop: the ditch
loop: Line 1: you're digging a ditch inside your own front door. Last: Ruth asks, very quietly, if she can sit in your ditch (the doubter now wants the thing she called crazy).
facts: Snow is mostly trapped air and insulates well; an igloo warmed by body heat alone can sit between about -7 C and +16 C inside while it is far colder outside (Wikipedia 'Igloo'; verify wording before voice). 'Almost forty degrees warmer' is within that range against -40 outside.
Igloos have a small vent hole in the roof, and a sunken entrance (a cold trap) because cold air sinks and stays below the sleeping level (Wikipedia 'Igloo'; verify before voice).
Forty below is the same in Celsius and Fahrenheit.
Tent poles snapping in a long blizzard and a battery heater dying: scenario logic, exaggerated for comedy.

lines.narration: You're digging a ditch inside your own front *door*.
lines.scene: Wide on a snow dome at dusk; you, waist-deep in a trench that runs under the doorway, flinging snow out.
lines.camera: Low push-in along the trench
lines.gag: You slide down it on your belly like a penguin

lines.narration: Because your plane is stuck on a mountain, it's forty below, and rescue is a week *away*.
lines.scene: Pull back over the ridge: a small plane nose-down in a snowdrift, unharmed but stuck, its propeller bent like a pretzel; endless peaks, no roads.
lines.camera: Fast pull-out with motion-blur streaks to an extreme wide
lines.gag: The bent propeller slowly droops

lines.narration: The other survivor is Captain Ruth. She's flown for 40 years, and she has a *manual*.
lines.scene: Ruth in a flight cap and scarf, sitting in the plane's open door, licking a finger to turn a page.
lines.camera: Telephoto from your dome to the plane
lines.gag: The manual is as thick as a phone book, with 200 sticky notes
lines.spoken: The other survivor is Captain Ruth. She's flown for forty years, and she has a manual.

lines.narration: She taps page 12. "Stay with the *aircraft*."
lines.scene: Insert on the page, then Ruth's flat face.
lines.camera: Hard cut insert, then MCU
lines.gag: Page 12 has a drawing of a smiling plane
lines.spoken: She taps page twelve. "Stay with the aircraft."

lines.narration: But you keep cutting snow blocks. Hour 1, ten. Hour 3, forty. By sunset, a *dome*.
lines.spoken: But you keep cutting snow blocks. Hour one, ten. Hour three, forty. By sunset, a dome.
lines.scene: Three dissolves on the same framing as the sun drops: a ring of ten blocks, a waist-high spiral, a finished dome glowing pink in the dusk.
lines.camera: Locked framing with a slow creep-in across three dissolves
lines.gag: Each dissolve, Ruth in the plane door has moved three sticky notes further into the manual

lines.narration: So you poke a hole in the roof, on *purpose*.
lines.scene: You punch up through the dome with a ski pole; across the snow Ruth looks up from the manual.
lines.camera: Inside the dome looking up, then a reverse wide
lines.gag: The puff of snow lands on Ruth's reading glasses

lines.narration: And the door? You dig it lower than the floor, like a little *ditch*.
lines.scene: The tunnel entrance sinks below floor level; cross-section cut-away of the dome.
lines.camera: Cross-section cut-away
lines.gag: The callback: you belly-slide down it again, slower

lines.narration: Ruth flips to page 40. "Do not sleep in a *hole*."
lines.scene: Insert on the manual, then Ruth raising one eyebrow.
lines.camera: Insert, then CU
lines.gag: Page 40 is a drawing of you
lines.spoken: Ruth flips to page forty. "Do not sleep in a hole."

lines.narration: That night, the plane's steel walls tick as they *freeze*.
lines.scene: Night: the plane under stars, frost creeping across its windows.
lines.camera: Slow push on the fuselage
lines.gag: Each tick pops a tiny 'tick' card off the hull

lines.narration: You sleep next to one tiny *candle*.
lines.scene: Inside the dome, warm candlelight on the ice blocks.
lines.camera: Top-down on you curled up by the candle
lines.gag: Your breath makes little clouds shaped like the candle flame

lines.narration: Then, on day 3, a blizzard hits, and it doesn't *stop*.
lines.spoken: [tense] Then, on day three, a blizzard hits, and it doesn't stop.
lines.scene: White-out: snow blasting sideways across the ridge, the plane half buried, the two shelters barely visible.
lines.camera: Wide, camera rocked by gusts, impact kicks on each gust
lines.gag: The plane's bent propeller spins the wrong way in the wind

lines.narration: The wind howls for two days. The plane rocks. Snow fills every vent. One. Two. *Three*.
lines.scene: Storm: the plane rocking, vents packing with snow one by one.
lines.camera: Three hard-cut inserts, one per vent
lines.gag: Each vent clogs with a cartoon 'thunk' of snow

lines.narration: And steel does what steel does. It pulls the heat out of everything it *touches*.
lines.scene: Inside the cabin: frost spreading from the walls toward Ruth, wrapped in every blanket.
lines.camera: Slow arc around Ruth, frost racing in
lines.gag: Ruth's breath freezes into a little ice sculpture of a plane

lines.narration: Her blankets freeze to the *wall*.
lines.scene: Ruth peels away from the wall; the blanket stays there, frozen in her shape.
lines.camera: Hard cut on 'wall'
lines.gag: Ruth tries to stand and the blanket stays stuck, upright like a ghost

lines.narration: Meanwhile, inside your house of ice, you just took off your *jacket*.
lines.scene: Inside the igloo: calm, golden candlelight, you in your striped tee sipping melted snow from a mug, jacket folded beside you. Muffled storm outside.
lines.camera: Slow arc around you
lines.gag: You're reading the plane's safety card like a magazine

lines.narration: You see, snow is mostly trapped air, and trapped air works like a giant puffy *blanket*.
lines.scene: Macro on a snow block: a glowing cut-away shows tiny air pockets between the crystals, like a sponge.
lines.camera: Macro push into the snow block
lines.gag: The air pockets are drawn as tiny sleeping faces

lines.narration: The roof hole lets old air out, and the ditch traps the cold, because cold air *sinks*.
lines.scene: Cross-section again: a soft warm-orange glow fills the dome and drifts out of the roof hole; blue cold air pours into the ditch and pools there like water.
lines.camera: Side-on cut-away, tilt from the roof hole down to the ditch
lines.gag: The cold air pools in the ditch like a blue puddle

lines.narration: So one candle and your body heat make it almost forty degrees warmer in *here*.
lines.scene: Split by the ice wall: inside golden and calm, outside white and screaming; a little thermometer on each side.
lines.camera: Slow lateral glide through the wall from inside to outside
lines.gag: The outside thermometer is frozen solid

lines.narration: Then, something knocks on your *wall*.
lines.spoken: [tense, hushed] Then, something knocks on your wall.
lines.scene: Inside: three soft thumps; snow dust falls from the ceiling; you freeze mid-sip.
lines.camera: Punch close-up on you, hard cut
lines.gag: Snow dust sprinkles into your mug

lines.narration: It's Ruth, holding the manual, open to a page called *igloos*.
lines.scene: Ruth at the tunnel mouth, frosted eyebrows, manual held up like a menu.
lines.camera: Your POV from inside the dome
lines.gag: The sticky note on that page says 'SKIP'

lines.narration: She asks, very quietly, if she can sit in your *ditch*.
lines.scene: Ruth, already crouched in the ditch before you answer.
lines.camera: CU on Ruth's face, the dome glowing behind her
lines.gag: An icicle hangs off Ruth's nose
